meta.title: Assumptions and scenarios — kept separate from observations
meta.rule: The brief asks for observations and assumptions to be distinguished. Everything in this file is an ASSUMPTION. It is not a finding, it is not sourced, and it is never presented as a value on any other page. The calculator requires the user to type these in.

scenarios.name: Business as usual
scenarios.premise: Tenant performs through expiry, renews or is replaced at or near market, cap rates hold, no capital event larger than routine maintenance.
scenarios.what_changes: Rent grows on the lease schedule; property tax grows no faster than the Proposition 13 cap of 2% absent a change of ownership.
scenarios.what_is_assumed: That the tenant renews. That is an assumption, not a fact, and it is the single most important one in the file.
scenarios.observable_that_would_disconfirm: A notice of non-renewal, or inclusion of the unit in a closure programme.

scenarios.name: Rate and cap-rate normalisation
scenarios.premise: Cap rates move against the owner because long rates rise or because lenders price short-lease single-tenant risk wider.
scenarios.what_changes: Value moves inversely with the cap rate. A 50 basis point move on a 5.50% cap is roughly an 8% value change before any income change.
scenarios.what_is_assumed: The direction and size of the cap-rate move. Nothing in this repository supports a specific number, which is why the calculator asks for it.
scenarios.observable_that_would_disconfirm: Closed comparable trades at stable cap rates.
scenarios.verified_context_only: The U.S. 10-year Treasury par yield was 4.19% on 2 January 2026 per the U.S. Treasury daily yield curve; that is a rate observation, not a cap-rate forecast.

scenarios.name: Tenant credit event
scenarios.premise: The operator stops paying or vacates before expiry, inside a soft leasing market.
scenarios.what_changes: Rent stops, the owner carries taxes, insurance and security, and the site may need re-tenanting capex.
scenarios.what_is_assumed: The vacancy duration and re-tenanting cost. Both are user inputs in the calculator.
scenarios.observable_that_would_disconfirm: A confirmed renewal, or a guaranty from a stronger obligor than assumed.

scenarios.name: Black swan: regional catastrophe
scenarios.premise: A damaging earthquake, or a wildfire-driven regional insurance and power event, closes the unit for a period and reprices insurance across the region.
scenarios.what_changes: Loss of rent for the closure period, repair cost net of insurance, a higher premium afterwards, and a thinner buyer pool at exit.
scenarios.what_is_assumed: The closure length, the uninsured share, and the premium shock. No official source supplies these for this parcel, and they are inputs, not findings.
scenarios.observable_that_would_disconfirm: A parcel-specific hazard screen showing no special-flood or high-fire designation plus confirmed earthquake cover with a serviceable deductible.

scenarios.name: Black swan: Los Angeles-specific shock outside the property
scenarios.premise: A regional event that does not damage the building but damages demand: a prolonged entertainment or port disruption, a large employer exit, or a sustained out-migration.
scenarios.what_changes: Trade-area sales fall, tenant renewal appetite falls, and the cap rate a buyer will pay widens even if the building is intact.
scenarios.what_is_assumed: That such an event occurs and its magnitude. Not modelled numerically; it is a qualitative branch on the Risk page.
scenarios.observable_that_would_disconfirm: Sustained employment growth with sector diversification. The verified BLS data currently show exactly that pattern in part: health and education +3.8% offsetting information -5.7%.

calculator_defaults_notice: The calculator opens with illustrative numbers so that the mechanism is visible. Those numbers are labelled 'illustrative default — replace with your own' in the interface and are never used in any table, chart or sentence on this site.
